title: Clarifying words and changing your view

captions.physics: Exploring what was said through examples

meaning: Careful clarification helps you unfold uncertain words and see them differently, leaving time for an inward change of perspective.
text: An unclear sentence sometimes needs a fuller account before a quick reply. The Empress in the physical position of Vishuddha helps what was said unfold: asking for an example, describing a feeling and continuing the other person’s thought. The Moon in energy supports attentive exploration of an impression while it remains short of precise understanding. The Hanged Man in emotions responds with an inward pause. An earlier version no longer fits and another needs time. Conversation can be useful without requiring clarification to eliminate all uncertainty or produce an immediate shared judgement.

For example, discussing the weekend brings the words, “I want to go somewhere far away.” Detailed questions reveal a wish for quiet and freedom from urgent tasks more than distance. **Clarification can change the question you are discussing.** Choosing a distant place becomes talking about a day that would feel free. Someone may need time to release the first attractive idea, and that pause can remain understandable within the exchange.

The difficulty is becoming so interested in subtler meanings that a simple wish receives no answer. Each new version suspends the earlier one and agreement is postponed. Care towards uncertainty stays valuable but needs a connection to the spoken request. Naming what is clear already gives your conversation footing without demanding a final explanation of every feeling.
